# Review pack: Zakariyya

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/zakariyya.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The chapters are a reading order built from the ayat, not a chronology the Quran claims; surah order is not time order. The accounts overlap with Maryam's and with Yahya's; this draft states only what concerns Zakariyya. The same moment may be told in 3:38-41 and 19:2-11; the ayat do not say, and the chapters keep both. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Zakariyya, his trade and his death. None is used in this draft.
- The age and barrenness details (3:40, 19:4-5, 19:8) are given only as the ayat say them: old age has reached him, his bone has grown weak and his head has flared with white, his wife is barren. A scholar should decide whether the self-description in 19:4 is worded with enough care.
- The passages with the glad tidings and the sign (3:39-41 and 19:7-11) are not joined into one scene; the ayat speak of three days in one place and three nights in the other.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Zakariyya's wife, his kinship to Maryam, the trade attributed to him and his death. None is used.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The guardian of Maryam  (`#guardian-of-maryam`)

Cited ayat: 3:37

> **3:37** فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَٰمَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَا قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ

### Claims

**c1** (3:37): Zakariyya was made guardian of Maryam, whom her Lord had accepted with a good acceptance and caused to grow well.

**c2** (3:37): Whenever Zakariyya went in to her in the mihrab, he found provision with her, and he asked her where she had this from.

**c3** (3:37): She said that it is from God, and that God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning.

### One-minute summary

Zakariyya was made guardian of Maryam, and whenever he went in to her in the mihrab he found provision with her, which she said was from God [c1][c2][c3].

### Complete story

Zakariyya was made guardian of Maryam, whom her Lord had accepted with a good acceptance and caused to grow well [c1]. Whenever Zakariyya went in to her in the mihrab, he found provision with her, and he asked her where she had this from [c2]. She said that it is from God, and that God gives provision to whom He wills without reckoning [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah names Zakariyya as her guardian and as the one who went in to her [c1][c2]. The question about the provision is his, and the answer is hers [c2][c3]. This draft states only what concerns Zakariyya here; the rest of Maryam's account is in her own entry [c1].

### Kids mode

Zakariyya looked after Maryam [c1]. When he went in to her, he found food and drink with her, and she told him it was from God [c2][c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Maryam's answer places her provision with God, who gives to whom He wills [c3]. A reader may notice that Zakariyya asks about what he finds and receives an answer that points to God [c2][c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the provision was, or how it came; the ayah says only provision.
- Not established: how Zakariyya was related to Maryam, or how long he was her guardian; the ayah does not say.
- Not established: whether the Arabic wording makes God or Zakariyya the one acting in kaffalaha; this draft says that Zakariyya was made her guardian, and the reviewer checks the recitation.
- Not established: where the mihrab was or what it was.

## 2. The secret prayer  (`#the-secret-prayer`)

Cited ayat: 3:38, 19:2-6

> **3:38** هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ

> **19:2** ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُۥ زَكَرِيَّآ
>
> **19:3** إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ نِدَآءً خَفِيًّا
>
> **19:4** قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَهَنَ ٱلْعَظْمُ مِنِّى وَٱشْتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا وَلَمْ أَكُنۢ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا
>
> **19:5** وَإِنِّى خِفْتُ ٱلْمَوَٰلِىَ مِن وَرَآءِى وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًا فَهَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّا
>
> **19:6** يَرِثُنِى وَيَرِثُ مِنْ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ وَٱجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (3:38): There Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking for good offspring from Him, and said that God hears supplication.

**c2** (19:2-3): The ayah is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya, when he called on his Lord with a hidden call.

**c3** (19:4): He said that his bone had grown weak and his head had flared with white, and that he had never been unfortunate in calling on his Lord.

**c4** (19:5-6): He said that he feared the kinsfolk who would come after him, and that his wife was barren, and asked God for an heir from Himself who would inherit from him and from the family of Yaqub, and to make him pleasing.

### One-minute summary

Zakariyya called on his Lord in a hidden call for good offspring, speaking of his weakness, his fear for what would come after him, and his wife's barrenness [c1][c2][c3][c4].

### Complete story

There Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking for good offspring from Him, and said that God hears supplication [c1]. The ayah is a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zakariyya, when he called on his Lord with a hidden call [c2]. He said that his bone had grown weak and his head had flared with white, and that he had never been unfortunate in calling on his Lord [c3]. He said that he feared the kinsfolk who would come after him, and that his wife was barren, and asked God for an heir from Himself who would inherit from him and from the family of Yaqub, and to make him pleasing [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat give the prayer in different forms: a short request for good offspring (3:38) and a longer one that speaks of his weakness, his fear and his wife (19:4-6) [c1][c3][c4]. The longer form is introduced as a mention of the mercy of his Lord to His servant [c2]. The word for his hidden call means a call made quietly [c2].

### Kids mode

Zakariyya called quietly to his Lord and asked for a child to come after him [c1][c2][c4]. He said that he had never been unhappy when he called on his Lord [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The prayer begins with the speaker's weakness and his history of calling on God, before he asks for anything [c3]. A reader may notice that the prayer is described as a hidden call and as a mercy [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: Zakariyya's age, or the age or name of his wife, or how long she had been barren; the ayat give none of these.
- Not established: who the kinsfolk are or what he feared from them.
- Not established: what the heir was to inherit, whether property, prophethood or knowledge; the ayah says only from him and from the family of Yaqub.
- Not established: where or when he prayed beyond the setting of the preceding verse; the ayat give no further detail.

## 3. The good news  (`#the-glad-tidings`)

Cited ayat: 3:39-40, 19:7-9

> **3:39** فَنَادَتْهُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآئِمٌ يُصَلِّى فِى ٱلْمِحْرَابِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَىٰ مُصَدِّقًۢا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
>
> **3:40** قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌ وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِىَ ٱلْكِبَرُ وَٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرٌ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ

> **19:7** يَٰزَكَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ ٱسْمُهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا
>
> **19:8** قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌ وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا
>
> **19:9** قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْـًٔا

### Claims

**c1** (3:39): The angels called to him while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous.

**c2** (3:40): He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren; the answer was that in this way God does what He wills.

**c3** (19:7): He was addressed by name as Zakariyya and told that God gives him good news of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom God had not made a namesake before.

**c4** (19:8): He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached the extreme of old age.

**c5** (19:9): The answer was that it is so, that his Lord says it is easy for Him, and that He had created him before when he was nothing.

### One-minute summary

Zakariyya was given good news of a boy named Yahya, and asked how this could be when old age had reached him and his wife was barren; the answer was that God does what He wills [c2][c3][c4][c5].

### Complete story

The angels called to him while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren; the answer was that in this way God does what He wills [c2]. He was addressed by name as Zakariyya and told that God gives him good news of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom God had not made a namesake before [c3]. He said, my Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached the extreme of old age [c4]. The answer was that it is so, that his Lord says it is easy for Him, and that He had created him before when he was nothing [c5].

### Deep study

Both passages give good news, a question from Zakariyya, and an answer from God [c1][c2][c3][c4][c5]. In 3:39 the good news comes from the angels, in 19:7 it is given in the voice of God; the ayat do not say whether this is the same moment [c1][c3]. The question is the same in each place and refers to old age and to his wife being barren [c2][c4]. The answers are that God does what He wills, and that creating him from nothing was easy for God [c2][c5].

### Kids mode

Zakariyya was told that he would have a boy named Yahya [c1][c3]. He asked how this could be, since he was old and his wife could not have a child [c2][c4]. He was told that God does what He wills and that it is easy for Him [c2][c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The question about how it can be is answered by pointing to God's will and to God's earlier creation of the questioner [c2][c5]. A reader may notice that the question is asked plainly and that the answer is also given plainly [c2][c4][c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who speaks the answers in 3:40 and 19:9; the verb is he said with no named speaker.
- Not established: whether 3:39 and 19:7 describe the same moment, or whether the angels of 3:39 are the voice of 19:7.
- Not established: Zakariyya's age, or how old his wife was; the ayat say old age and barren, nothing more.
- Not established: the sense of the word for one who holds back, or of the word for namesake, which can also read as equal; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: an identification of the word from God in 3:39 with a person; it is not used in the story texts.

## 4. The sign  (`#the-sign-of-silence`)

Cited ayat: 3:41, 19:10-11

> **3:41** قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةً قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمْزًا وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ كَثِيرًا وَسَبِّحْ بِٱلْعَشِىِّ وَٱلْإِبْكَٰرِ

> **19:10** قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةً قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا
>
> **19:11** فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْمِحْرَابِ فَأَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُوا۟ بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا

### Claims

**c1** (3:41): Zakariyya said, my Lord, make a sign for me; the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three days except by gesture, and that he should remember his Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the early morning.

**c2** (19:10): He said, my Lord, make a sign for me; the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three nights, sawiyyan, a word whose sense is left open here.

**c3** (19:11): He went out to his people from the mihrab and signalled to them to glorify God in the morning and the evening.

### One-minute summary

Zakariyya asked for a sign and was told that for three days he would not speak to people except by gesture; he went out from the mihrab and signalled to his people to glorify God morning and evening [c1][c3].

### Complete story

Zakariyya said, my Lord, make a sign for me; the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three days except by gesture, and that he should remember his Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the early morning [c1]. In the other passage the answer was that his sign would be that he would not speak to people for three nights, sawiyyan, a word whose sense is left open here [c2]. He went out to his people from the mihrab and signalled to them to glorify God in the morning and the evening [c3].

### Deep study

One passage names days and the other names nights, and the ayat do not say how they relate [c1][c2]. In the first passage the sign comes with an instruction to remember God much and to glorify Him [c1]. The signal to his people in the last ayah is a call to glorify God [c3].

### Kids mode

Zakariyya asked God for a sign [c1]. For three days he would not speak to people, except by gesture [c1]. He went out and signalled to his people to glorify God morning and evening [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The sign of silence is joined to a command to remember and glorify God much [c1]. A reader may notice that when he comes out to his people, his gesture calls them to glorify God as well [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: why the sign took this form, or whether it was a limit on his speech or an inability; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: whether the three days of 3:41 and the three nights of 19:10 are the same period; the ayat do not join them.
- Not established: how he signalled, or whether he could still speak to God or glorify; the ayat do not say.
- Not established: the sense of sawiyyan; it is read as sound, whole or unbroken, and the reviewer decides the wording.

## 5. Answered, and named among the righteous  (`#answered-and-named`)

Cited ayat: 21:89-90, 6:85

> **21:89** وَزَكَرِيَّآ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِى فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْوَٰرِثِينَ
>
> **21:90** فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُۥ زَوْجَهُۥٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ

> **6:85** وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحْيَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَإِلْيَاسَ كُلٌّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (21:89): Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking not to be left alone, and said that God is the best of inheritors.

**c2** (21:90): God answered him, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him.

**c3** (21:90): The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him.

**c4** (6:85): Zakariyya and Yahya are named, with others, each described as being among the righteous.

### One-minute summary

Zakariyya called on his Lord not to leave him alone, and God answered him, gave him Yahya and put his wife right for him [c1][c2].

### Complete story

Zakariyya called on his Lord, asking not to be left alone, and said that God is the best of inheritors [c1]. God answered him, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him [c2]. The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him [c3]. Zakariyya and Yahya are named, with others, each described as being among the righteous [c4].

### Deep study

The call in 21:89 is brief and ends by naming God as the best of inheritors [c1]. The answer has parts: the gift of Yahya and the putting right of his wife [c2]. The description in the plural that follows does not say who is included [c3]. In 6:85 Zakariyya and Yahya are named among those each described as righteous [c4].

### Kids mode

Zakariyya asked God not to leave him alone [c1]. God answered him and gave him Yahya [c2]. Zakariyya and Yahya are named among the righteous [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The ayat show a prayer made in need and an answer that gives what was asked [c1][c2]. They also describe those spoken of as hastening to good, calling on God in hope and fear, and humble before Him [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what put his wife right means, or whether it refers to her barrenness; the ayah does not say how.
- Not established: who they are in 21:90, whether Zakariyya, his wife and Yahya or others; the plural is not explained.
- Not established: the time between his call and the answer, or how long the answer took.
- Not established: why the others named in 6:85 are grouped with them; this draft states only the part that concerns Zakariyya and Yahya.
